title: Smoothies stay fresh but ice cannot be blended into the recipe & every ingredient has to be bite-sized before blending
text:
Smoothies stay fresh but ice cannot be blended into the recipe & every ingredient has to be bite-sized before blending. After having tried this, I am actually disappointed I ordered this because it is not as versatile as my old blender or my [[ASIN:B00NGV3X2W Nutri Ninja Auto-iQ Blender]].

WHAT's IN THE BOX
- Main blender unit
- Blending jar with lid
- Vacuum storage jar with lid
- Two extra vacuum plugs

Each lid is 3 pieces (the filter, vacuum plug, and the lid housing). The blending jar is supposed to have a detachable blade but I was unable to remove it. Since it is sharp, I just used a brush inside the unit to clean.

LIKES
- The vacuum seal - removes the oxygen from the jars to keep ingredients at least color fresh which supposedly tastes fresher.
- Due to less air there is a reduction of foam on top and the blend is smoother.
- There's a cord wrap underneath the unit.
- The storage jar allows me to keep things fresh (after it's vacuum sealed) if not consuming immediately.
- The auto button allows me to set and forget with vacuuming and blending combined.
- There's an option to pulse if more blending is needed.
- There's an option to manually blend.
- The unit will not work unless blending jar is locked in position; in fact a continous beep occurs.
- The unit has non-skid suction feet but it did not adhere on my counter top glass but it did adhere to my counter without the glass.
- Register online and you'll get a 2-year warranty (doubled from 1 year)
- A tiny bare-bones recipe booklet is included.

DISLIKES
- The unit is too large (at 18 inches tall) for under counter storage (see picture).
- All ingredients have to be cut into small pieces.
- Ice (or anything hard) cannot be used in the blender.
- I was not able to remove the 6-blade assembly from the blending jar. This might not be an issue for some but it was for me. However, I do not care as I use a bottle brush to clean out the blade area with the unit intact.
- The blender cannot be run continuously for more than 3 minutes; motor burnout is likely to occur.
- Ingredients over 104 degrees should not be put in the blending jar, which means soup ingredients have to cool down first.
- The recipe booklet sometimes left me with questions, such as adding pre-soaked cashews to a recipe without saying how long they have to be pre-soaked (Page 36). Yet a few pages later it says almonds have to be soaked for 8 hours for another recipe.
- I have to be careful not to lift the unit by the top because the shape of it makes me want to do this. Also, the top of the main unit does not flip over enough. It keeps wanting to close on itself. Therefore, I have to hold the top while I am trying to insert and lock the blender into place.

Note that everything has to be added all at once starting with liquid ingredients first. There's no option to add ingredients as it blends because that would break the vacuum seal.

Since I did not have the ingredients for the recipes on hand, I did blend some strawberries with milk and the color was rich and the drink was smooth without all the foam a non-vacuum blender. It also tasted great. Nevertheless, because I could not add ice to the blend, it was warm even though the ingredients came out of the refrigerator. Adding ice cubes to the blending ingredients just doesn't have the same mouth feel and refreshing taste. This and the fact that I have to cut up the ingredients into small pieces are my main dislikes. I am also disappointed that I need to hold the top cover as I am locking the blending jar into place as it requires a bit of coordination.
